metadata.source: RBI FinTech Department, Consumer Education and Protection Department (CEPD)

digital_banking_units_dbu.announcement: Announced in Union Budget 2022-23 by Union Finance Minister
digital_banking_units_dbu.target: Setting up 75 Digital Banking Units (DBUs) in 75 districts of the country to commemorate 75 years of Indian Independence (Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav)
digital_banking_units_dbu.dedication: Dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 16, 2022
digital_banking_units_dbu.nature: Specialized fixed-point business unit/hub housing certain minimal digital banking infrastructure for delivering digital banking products & services

zones.self_service_zone: 24x7x365 access to Cash Deposit Machines (CDM), Cash Recyclers, Passbook printing kiosk, Internet banking kiosk, and tab-banking
zones.assisted_zone: Manned by bank staff during working hours to assist customers with digital onboarding, account opening, KYC updates, and financial literacy

digital_banking_units_dbu.eligibility: Scheduled Commercial Banks (other than Regional Rural Banks, Payment Banks, and Local Area Banks) having past digital banking experience are permitted to open DBUs in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres without prior RBI approval.

digital_lending_framework.notification_date: RBI Guidelines issued on September 2, 2022 (recommendations of Working Group headed by Jayant Kumar Dash)

key_actors.regulated_entities_res: Commercial Banks, Primary UCBs, State & District Central Co-op Banks, and NBFCs
key_actors.lending_service_providers_lsps: Third-party agents of REs carrying out borrower acquisition, underwriting pricing, servicing, or recovery
key_actors.digital_lending_apps_dlas: Mobile and web-based applications used by REs or LSPs to offer digital lending products

core_mandates.detail: All loan disbursements and repayments must be executed directly between the bank account of the borrower and the RE, WITHOUT any pass-through or pool account of any third-party LSP.

REs must provide a standardized Key Fact Statement to the borrower before loan execution, stating all-inclusive cost of the loan (Annual Percentage Rate - APR), recovery agent details, and cooling-off period.

A mandatory period during which the borrower can exit the digital loan by paying the principal and proportionate APR without any prepayment penalty. Minimum 3 days for loans of tenor >= 7 days, and 1 day for loans of tenor < 7 days.
DLAs cannot access mobile phone resources like contact lists, call logs, media files, or biometric data. One-time access to camera and microphone is permitted only for video KYC.

neo_banks_ecosystem.definition: FinTech firms that offer digital-only financial services without any physical branch network.
neo_banks_ecosystem.regulatory_status_in_india: RBI has NOT issued standalone digital banking or neo-banking licences. In India, Neo-banks are NOT banks under Section 5(b) of BR Act.
neo_banks_ecosystem.operating_model: Partner Banking Model — Neo-banks build user interfaces, apps, and analytics, while underlying accounts, regulatory compliance, and deposits are hosted with licensed partner Scheduled Commercial Banks (e.g., Federal Bank, SBM Bank, Equitas SFB).

integrated_ombudsman_scheme.official_name: The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 (RB-IOS, 2021)
integrated_ombudsman_scheme.launched_on: November 12, 2021 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi
schemes_integrated: The Ombudsman Scheme for Digital Transactions, 2019
entities_covered: Non-scheduled Urban Co-operative Banks with deposit size of ₹50 Crore and above
All Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) with deposit-taking permission or asset size of ₹100 Crore and above
All System Participants (Payment System Operators like NPCI, wallet providers)
integrated_ombudsman_scheme.portal_and_crpc: Complaints filed online via Complaint Management System (CMS portal: cms.rbi.org.in). RBI established the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC) at RBI Chandigarh for physical and email receipt.

compensation_powers.maximum_pecuniary_compensation: Up to ₹20,00,000 (₹20 Lakh) for actual loss suffered by the complainant directly arising out of the act or omission of the regulated entity
compensation_powers.mental_agony_compensation: Up to ₹1,00,000 (₹1 Lakh) for loss of complainant's time, expenses incurred, and harassment/mental anguish suffered

integrated_ombudsman_scheme.appellate_authority: Executive Director in charge of Consumer Education and Protection Department (CEPD) at RBI
integrated_ombudsman_scheme.appeal_time_limit: 30 days from the date of receipt of communication of the award or rejection of complaint

exam_traps.trap: Assuming Neo-banks in India have separate banking licences from RBI.
exam_traps.fact: Neo-banks do NOT hold banking licences in India. They operate exclusively via partner model with licensed commercial banks.

exam_traps.trap: Thinking maximum compensation under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman is ₹10 Lakh.
exam_traps.fact: Maximum pecuniary compensation is ₹20 Lakh, plus up to ₹1 Lakh for mental agony and loss of time.

exam_traps.trap: Believing Digital Lending Apps can access contact lists and photo galleries for recovery.
exam_traps.fact: RBI Digital Lending Guidelines explicitly PROHIBIT DLAs from accessing contact lists, call logs, and storage.
